# PR85 native driver transaction fixtures (Windows execution pending)

Use a separately authorized disposable snapshot, approved source-verified CA/wixlib/extension with core inputs matching this archive (fixture-only updates reuse that chain), and a signed nonboot package with complete actual INF-referenced payload approved for that baseline. Do not use forced historical boot-driver downgrades. No fixture is referenced by shipping Product.

`pr85-driver-failure.wxi` retains shipping InstallExecute `NOT Installed`. Existing strict before/after-old-removal fixtures remain separate from following independent native probe product.

Build `pr85-native-driver-transaction.wxs` with candle `-arch x64` or x86, `-ext <new DrvInstExt.dll>`, and definitions:

- `DriverFixtureSource`: one official directory containing unmodified signed `<name>.inf/.sys` and every actual INF-referenced support file. Validate SourceDisksFiles/CopyFiles completeness before admission; INF/CAT/SYS alone is not sufficient.
- `DriverFixtureName`: actual INF/SYS basename, e.g. approved viorng.
- `DriverFixtureSupportFile` (optional): one support-file **basename**, copied from the same `DriverFixtureSource` directory into the same driver component. Official285 VIORNG requires `-dDriverFixtureSupportFile=viorngum.dll`; balloon omits this definition. Do not alter INF/CAT/SYS, fabricate a triplet or omit any remaining required dependency. Reject admission if this small fixture cannot express the complete payload.
- `DriverFixtureCatalog`: full path of actual signed `<name>.cat`; for genuine signature-error case ONLY, `pr85-invalid-catalog.txt` instead. Destination name remains `<name>.cat`; signed INF unchanged.
Architecture fixes ProgramFiles, Win64 and a distinct per-architecture component GUID in fixture source.
- `DriverFixtureFault`: `afterNative` or `none`.

Light must also reference same approved source-verified extension. Package GUID is generated; record actual MSI SHA/ProductCode/PackageCode. This probe deliberately has unconditional test-only InstallExecute so maintenance/uninstall effects run before its Type19 fault; it is not evidence that shipping InstallExecute may lose NOT Installed. Inspect generated tables before executing. InstallExecute < PR85_NativeFixtureFailure < InstallFinalize must be strict. Never edit installed/cached MSI.

Run `pr85-native-driver-transaction.ps1` elevated, one operation per invocation, with unique report directory. Script snapshots actual hardware, signed bindings/package identities and six module-owned metadata fields (including immutable INF/catalog hashes), starts native msiexec, captures exit/log/state, and stops. It never reboots, retries, repairs or restores baseline. Baseline equality permits OEM alias renumbering by comparing INF identities; parent must additionally check actual signed catalog/section witnesses and normal installer/component ownership with authoritative runtime harness. A successful script is not whole-system acceptance.

Bounded cases, each from independently identified baseline:

1. **Newly created package rollback:** genuinely absent approved signed optional package; build fault probe; `-Operation Install -FailAfterNative -ExpectedExit 1603`. Require log createdByThisCall=1, actual binding work when hardware exists, restored original bindings/sections/NULL-driver, removed newly published package, preserved hardware and metadata baseline.
2. **Preexisting package rollback:** package already exists, established by supported read-only capture or separately approved `pnputil /add-driver` preparation without `/install`; same fault install. Require createdByThisCall=0, no removal of preexisting package, original binding and typed metadata restored. Include genuine no-matching-hardware case: signed staging succeeds, zero binding attempts, no ERROR_NO_SUCH_DEVINST failure normalization.
3. **Owned uninstall inverse:** normal successful probe install from absent-package baseline with `-ExpectedExit 0`; separately invoke same source-built fault-capable probe `-Operation Uninstall -FailAfterNative -ExpectedExit 1603`. Require actual known-created removal, MSI restoring signed source files before inverse, real restaging and exact prior binding restoration. OEM alias may change. Do not mistake metadata-only or retained no-op for removal.
4. **Nonowned uninstall:** successful probe installed over preexisting external package records no createdByComponent ownership. Ordinary uninstall must remove only its module metadata/files and preserve external package/bindings.
5. **Native error propagation:** independently absent package, build with invalid catalog input, no Type19 requested; `-Operation Install -ExpectedExit 1603`. Prove real signature/staging failure is first causal failure, checked MSI error, no binding/metadata mutation, and baseline equality. A preexisting exact INF can take ERROR_FILE_EXISTS instead; reject that case as a signature-error witness.

6. **NONBOOT already-better balloon driver stays bound:** use independently identified baseline with a present balloon device already bound to a demonstrably better signed driver. Confirm BALLOON is nonboot (not Boot/System start); do not use viostor/vioscsi or force any binding. Build the existing probe with `DriverFixtureName=balloon`, unmodified **official older signed** balloon INF/CAT/SYS matching this OS/architecture, its real catalog, and `DriverFixtureFault=none`. Record official provenance, file hashes and source INF DriverVer; do not tamper with source/signatures or execute an older installer. Before/after, capture `pnputil /enum-devices /instanceid "<actual balloon instance>" /drivers` output for Windows-reported candidate rank/date/version and selected driver. Run existing script once with `-DriverName balloon -Operation Install -ExpectedExit 0` (or explicitly expected documented 3010). Require at least one real target rank witness, `RankedBindingsUnchanged=true`, and identical actual balloon package identity/version/DEVPKEY_Device_DriverRank before/after. Older package may be staged, but better driver must stay bound; staging/metadata changes mean whole-state equality is not required for this successful case. After staging, compare actual candidate ranks/date/version from pnputil, not an assumed "older means lower rank" label. Native API must use flags0, never FORCE_INF. This case is **runtime pending**, not a host-test Windows proof.

Parent owns hardware/boot safety, baseline selection and first-red stop. No Windows cases were executed in source phase. Historical and new modern predecessor omission/identity-transition admission, shared/default/damaged handoff, nested boundary, rollback-disabled policy, cancellation, reboot/retry and x86 runtime remain required outside this small probe.

Focused P1/P2 source regressions are executed in `driver_alias_prefix_test.cpp`: production read-only resolution with A owning P, B re-aliasing P forward/rollback, old OEM reused by Q, missing Store hints and subsequent A lookup; ambiguous/missing/unknown identity fails closed without creator transfer. Production whole-WCHAR-prefix/frame/reverse-dispatch code is injected with odd-byte, short-read and failed-read tails after completed attempted work; cleanup must not run and first error persists. These tests do not exercise Windows driver APIs or hardware. Actual x64 rebuild/reviewer recheck and narrow nonboot runtime remain next gates; no production test hooks added.
